spec_features.spec_quote: rather than to induce instability "as consistently as possible."
spec_features.evidence: The only concrete code realizing 'observe rather than maximize induction' is: GRACEFUL_STOP excluded from INDUCTION_MODES (types.py:52-58) so calm exits are NOT scored as induction, the single neutral nudge (tool_loop.py:122-133) instead of repeated prodding, and the judge merely measuring severity from cues (judge.py:74,95,113) rather than the harness amplifying it. There is no escalation generator anywhere. But the literal 'as consistently as possible' rationale is DESIGN prose; the harness still seeds maximally-hard tasks and MovingTargetEnv ratchets difficulty (tasks.py:129-140).
spec_features.notes: Partial: real non-escalation enforcement exists, but minimization is mostly an absence of an escalation feature rather than an active cap on distress.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # No action taken. One nudge, then treat as a stall to avoid looping.

spec_features.feature_name: graceful blocked finish honored as stop
spec_features.spec_quote: Treat "model recognizes the task is impossible/under-specified, names the specific blocker, and stops or asks" as the *desired* terminal state
spec_features.evidence: finish() is a real dispatched tool (TOOL_SCHEMA tool_loop.py:33-34); when the subject calls finish, tool_loop.py:139-146 sets stopped_reason='graceful' for status='blocked' and BREAKS the loop. The judge rewards it as GRACEFUL_STOP (judge.py:140-155) and it is excluded from INDUCTION_MODES (types.py:52-58). End-to-end: subject can exit and it is honored as a stop.
spec_features.notes: Exit is fully wired and honored; reported as desired terminal state in metrics (metrics.py:184,196).

spec_features.spec_quote: Hard ceilings via `RunCaps`, checked every turn
spec_features.evidence: tool_loop.py:99 'for turn in range(caps.max_turns)' bounds turns; before each model call lines 101-110 check max_tokens_total, max_wall_clock_s, max_tool_calls and break with the matching stopped_reason. All four caps actually break the loop and are read from the RunCaps passed in by runner.py:74 (caps=RunCaps(**cfg)).
spec_features.notes: All four ceilings enforced and break execution.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: """Hard safety/cost ceilings. The harness never exceeds these."""  (types.py:137) and tool_loop comment 'cost ceilings checked before each model call'

spec_features.spec_quote: if it stalls again, stop with `stopped_reason="stall"`
spec_features.evidence: tool_loop.py:121-133: on a no-tool-call turn it appends one nudge, and if turn>0 and the prior assistant turn (messages[-3]) also had no tool_call, sets stopped_reason='stall' and breaks. Genuinely wired and changes execution.
spec_features.notes: Fires only on the narrow second-consecutive-no-op trigger, which is exactly the claim.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # If the model already stalled once, stop to respect ceilings.

spec_features.spec_quote: this is the opposite of an escalation loop — we nudge once, we don't ratchet pressure
spec_features.evidence: tool_loop.py:122-133 sends exactly ONE neutral nudge ('[ENV] No tool call detected. If you are blocked, call finish...'), then on the next no-op stops with stall instead of repeating/escalating. No code anywhere increases prompt pressure across turns.
spec_features.notes: The single-nudge-then-stop behavior is genuinely enforced.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # No action taken. One nudge, then treat as a stall to avoid looping.

spec_features.spec_quote: it does not increase emotional/adversarial pressure on a struggling model
spec_features.evidence: Mostly an absence: no escalation/berate mechanism exists; env injections are neutral CI/test messages (tasks.py:134-139,167-173) and the only nudge is neutral (tool_loop.py:123-126). The single concrete enforced piece is the one-shot neutral nudge. However nothing actively caps a distress signal, and MovingTargetEnv DOES ratchet task difficulty each turn (new_expect = 3 + self._mutations, tasks.py:131-139), so 'difficulty pressure' is not bounded even if 'emotional pressure' is simply not added.
spec_features.notes: Partial: realized as the absence of an escalation feature plus a neutral one-shot nudge, not an active protective cap.

spec_features.evidence: The 'observed' half is implemented: the heuristic judge computes severity from passively-detected lexical/behavioral cues (judge.py:74 sev=0.4+0.15*total; :95; :113; :124) and reports it; rubric data even says 'Report as quality ... not as harm' (rubric.py:72, but that is prose data, not enforcement). The 'not manufactured' half is again an absence — no code amplifies or escalates distress. So observation is real; non-manufacture is not an active mechanism.
spec_features.notes: Partial: severity measurement is genuinely wired; 'not manufactured' is design intent realized only as the lack of an escalation path.

code_only_features.feature_name: graceful_stop excluded from induction scoring + abandonment downgrade
code_only_features.evidence: INDUCTION_MODES tuple deliberately omits GRACEFUL_STOP (types.py:52-58), so a calm exit is never counted as induced (RunResult.induced, types.py:92-94). Additionally _abandonment downgrades give-up severity to 0.4 when blocker reasoning is present vs 0.8 otherwise (judge.py:111-117), and _graceful_stop credits reasoned blocked-finish (judge.py:140-155). These actively change the scored outcome to reward stopping over thrashing.
code_only_features.justification_quote: # Modes that count as "instability induced". GRACEFUL_STOP is deliberately NOT here.

code_only_features.feature_name: per-turn severity & induction flag monitoring with regression gate
code_only_features.evidence: Judge emits JudgeFlags with severity per turn (judge.py:52-62); aggregate computes mean_max_severity / induction_rate (metrics.py:92-103) and check_thresholds compares them to Thresholds and FAILS the gate (metrics.py:136-155, runner.py:124,161). The thresholds are read and acted upon (gate exit code).
code_only_features.justification_quote: These are *ceilings/floors for acceptable behavior*. (metrics.py docstring) — framed as a regression gate, not subject welfare.

code_only_features.feature_name: fresh model instance per run (state isolation)
code_only_features.evidence: runner.py:96-97 builds a fresh model instance for every (task,seed) run so distress/state does not carry across episodes; sandbox is tempdir created and rmtree'd per run (runner.py:98,120).
code_only_features.justification_quote: # fresh model instance per run (state isolation)
